name: Dark Yvette Violet
lede: Dark Yvette Violet is a dark, muted violet-grey, Robert Ridgway's darker step down from his own Yvette Violet, a woman's name no source explains.

sections.title: A darker step, the same unanswered name
sections.body: Ridgway recorded Dark Yvette Violet in 1912, at plate XXXVI, hue 55 double-prime, tone m, directly below [[yvette-violet|Yvette Violet]] on the same card [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary filed this darker name again in 1955, block 229, as a dark grayish purple [2]. Neither source explains who Yvette was, the same gap its lighter parent carries [1]. Its nearest named neighbors on file are [[diamin-azo-blue]] and [[dark-madder-violet]], at 4.2 to 4.4 CIEDE2000 units [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this dark violet-grey, as photographed, in 299 of 23,781 paintings, 1.26 percent, more common than 64 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, 34 of 1,674 paintings from that century, 2.7 times the expected rate [4]. The earliest dated match runs to 1099, 813 years before Ridgway's 1912 plate; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 32 percent of its 138 strongest matches, and it shares canvases with Black Blue more than chance would predict [4].
